audience.en: An Argentine couple (Martín, 27, and Sofía, 26) with USD 9,000 in savings planning a New Zealand working holiday from around September 2027, deciding when to apply, where to start and how long the money lasts.
audience.es: Una pareja argentina (Martín, 27, y Sofía, 26) con USD 9,000 ahorrados que planea un working holiday en Nueva Zelanda desde alrededor de septiembre de 2027 y decide cuándo solicitar, dónde empezar y cuánto le durará el dinero.

localeReason: Spanish serves this couple directly: they are Argentine, and reading the application timing, the per-person fee and funds rules, the insurance wording and the open issues in their own language helps them compare what they are told with the English-only Immigration New Zealand pages. It changes no rule, fee, date or amount.

fee_per_person.label: Working holiday visa fee per person: NZ$215 application + NZ$455 immigration levy + NZ$100 tourism levy (IVL); matching the fees-guide row to Argentines is our reading

funds_rule.label: Funds required to show (NZ$4,200 on the official page; per-person reading is our assumption)

weekly_take_home.label: Weekly take-home, 40 hours at the NZ$23.95 minimum wage, tax code M, ACC 1.75% (IRD IR340 table)

cash_at_arrival.label: Cash left at arrival from USD 9,000 after visas, placeholder insurance and assumed USD 1,300 flights each

funds_gap.label: Shortfall if the NZ$4,200-each funds must stay untouched (flights assumed; moves with flight price)

cash_after_one_offs.label: Cash after one-off costs, before weekly spending (assumed costs; 2% conversion allowance assumed)

planningAssumptions.people: Martín, 27, and Sofía, 26, Argentine citizens; USD 9,000 savings; arrival around Sept–Nov 2027 depending on the 2027 opening date (not announced as of 2026-11-08).
planningAssumptions.costs: One-way flights USD 1,300 each; 2% currency/card cost; temporary first-week stay NZ$350; food NZ$150 a week; transport NZ$60 a week; phones NZ$30 a month each; other NZ$80 a week; bedding, basics and clothes NZ$300; work clothes NZ$100; SIMs NZ$60; room cost the Grey Lynn listing of NZ$275 a week for two people (may not allow couples); work at minimum wage for 30 or 20 hours; first pay one week after starting; 9 weeks stand in for about 2 months. All are planner assumptions, not sourced.
planningAssumptions.rates: NZD/USD 0.55434 (6 Nov 2026, aggregator, unconfirmed); ARS 1,545.50 per USD (BCRA, 5 Nov 2026); tax brackets and the NZ$23.95 minimum wage assumed unchanged in 2027; ACC earners' levy 1.83% for 2027–28 (published); NZ$4,200 assumed per person; tax code M assumed.
planningAssumptions.recommendation: Apply the day the 2027 round opens, each partner separately; Auckland for the first 3–5 weeks then Central Otago from late November is the author's judgement, not an official recommendation; USD 9,000 is tight.

datePolicy: Pages were read on 2026-11-08 in the original run (fetch timestamps 2026-11-07 UTC) and that access date is kept for every source. Source dates (the 2026 opening on 24 September 2026, the May 2026 fees guide, bond data for 1 March to 31 August 2026, rates dated 5 and 6 November 2026) are not access dates. Copy editing and translation are not a refresh.
uncertainties: The 2027 opening date, any fee or quota change, and how quickly the 1,000 places fill are not known; no couple or partner provision was found.
Whether NZ$4,200 is per person, and whether it must stay in the account on arrival, is not stated on the official page; per person is an assumption.

The NZ$770 fee comes from the 'working holiday scheme' row of the May 2026 fees guide read as the rest-of-world band; the country fee tool on the Argentina page was not displayed, so the mapping is the author's inference. The extension fee (NZ$245 plus levies) is not shown separately for Argentines.

NZD/USD 0.55434 is from an aggregator because the Reserve Bank page returned an error; the BCRA rate is official but not labelled Com. A 3500; the blue and MEP dollar rates and current Argentine exchange rules for individuals were not researched.

Flights (USD 1,300 each), living costs, the 2% conversion cost and a couple sharing one NZ$275 room are unsourced assumptions; cash at arrival, the 10.2 weeks with zero income and the USD 740.86 gap move directly with the flight price.
Insurance uses one insurer's price (USD 815.36 per person for 52 weeks, arithmetic 13 × 62.72); whether Immigration New Zealand accepts it is unverified.

City rent medians were read by the run's worker and were not independently re-parsed in the recheck; Roomies listings are examples, not availability, with 'available from' dates and no posting dates; only the listing pages whose full addresses appear in the source list are linked (the other listing paths appear only in shortened form).

PAYE examples other than NZ$163.41 (IRD IR340) are the author's calculations, not IRD table lookups; tax code M for a working holiday visa and KiwiSaver ineligibility for a working holiday visa are the author's readings.

2027 minimum wage, 2027–28 tax brackets, public holidays 2027–28, the sick-leave qualifying period, tax-refund timing, bank details beyond ANZ, and care-sector job requirements for Sofía were not found.

The arithmetic recheck (64 money checks, 39 claim checks, 0 failures on the final run) was done by the same author with a separate script, not by an outside reviewer; an earlier one-cent rounding mismatch (NZ$7,063.53 vs NZ$7,063.54) was fixed.

provenance.sourceAccessMethod: Local files only. The README locale contract and VOICE-GUIDE were read first, then the run's index.html, sources.md and independent-check.md. No network research, build or publication during authoring. The Spanish page was translated from the English guide.
provenance.originalResearchAccessLimitations: The original research used plain HTTP fetch, with the fetch tool's managed-browser fallback for client-rendered Immigration New Zealand pages and some 404 fallbacks; no sign-in, cookies or user cookie file. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand page returned 403; BNZ returned 403; ASB, Westpac and Kiwibank were not read.
provenance.independentCheckDisposition: A separate Decimal-arithmetic script recomputed 64 money figures and 39 claims against the sources with 0 failures on the final run (15 failures on the first run: one real one-cent inconsistency, fixed, and the rest display-precision or wording issues in the check). It was run by the same author, not an outside person. It did not re-verify the tenancy medians and flagged the aggregator exchange rate, unsourced flights and living costs, the single insurer, the per-person NZ$4,200 assumption and the unknown 2027 dates; the guide keeps all of them.
